Name: narration_subspace_suppression
Title: Think in Shorthand: Separating a Narration Subspace from Computation to Suppress Performative Reasoning
Short Hypothesis: Reasoning models carry two largely separable residual-stream subspaces: a computation subspace that carries out and updates the latent answer, and a multi-dimensional narration subspace that governs verbose, human-facing presentation of already-computed results. Overthinking is over-activation of the narration subspace after computation is effectively done. The mathematical novelty over a single verbosity/length direction is that we construct a low-rank narration subspace ORTHOGONALIZED against the answer-carrying (computation) directions by construction, so suppression provably preserves the latent answer to first order; the pre-registered criterion for the idea collapsing into prior length steering is that the narration subspace's top direction aligns with a reproduced single verbosity direction (principal angle < 20 degrees) AND projecting out the extra dimensions adds < 5% token reduction at matched accuracy. Suppressing narration while leaving computation intact makes the model think in shorthand, cutting tokens more precisely than a single direction.
Related Work: Recent work establishes that CoT is often performative or unfaithful and that latent answers form early: Reasoning Theater (2026) probes performative CoT and early-exits; TTS / 'Can Aha Moments Be Fake?' (2025) labels steps decorative vs load-bearing and finds a single steerable TrueThinking direction; State over Tokens (2025) reframes tokens as externalized state; Causal Bypass / CMI (2026) shows answers can be causally independent of CoT text; functional-metacognition work decodes single state factors (uncertainty, difficulty, task-type) as separate directions. Efficiency-steering work (Manifold Steering, CREST, ThinkEdit, ASC) steers a single verbosity/length direction. The differences, by objective / intervention / causal claim: TTS labels steps and steers one direction; verbosity steering pushes one length direction; functional-metacognition reads single scalar factors; none constructs a MULTI-DIMENSIONAL subspace decomposition of the residual stream into a computation subspace that must be preserved and a separable narration subspace that can be projected out. Our contribution is (1) constructing and causally validating these subspaces via contrastive activation collection (terse vs verbose renderings of identical computations) plus explicit orthogonalization against the answer-probe directions - which yields a genuinely different object from a verbosity direction because it is defined relative to, and removed from, the computation subspace rather than to output length; (2) showing overthinking corresponds to sustained narration-subspace activation after computation completes; (3) a training-free projection intervention finer-grained than a single length direction.
Abstract: Reasoning language models routinely 'overthink,' generating verbose chains of thought long after they have effectively solved a problem, inflating tokens, latency, and serving cost. Prior interpretability work explains this as performative or decorative reasoning and either labels steps or steers a single verbosity direction. We propose a sharper, dimensional account: the residual stream contains two largely separable subspaces - a computation subspace that performs and updates the latent answer, and a multi-dimensional narration subspace that governs verbose, human-facing presentation of already-computed results. We hypothesize that overthinking is sustained narration-subspace activation after computation completes, and that suppressing narration while preserving the orthogonal computation subspace lets the model think in shorthand with minimal accuracy loss. We construct the narration subspace via contrastive activation collection - rendering identical computations tersely versus verbosely - followed by difference-of-means, SVD, and orthogonalization against the answer-probe directions, so it is by construction distinct from a length direction. Across GSM8K, MATH500, AIME, and GPQA on DeepSeek-R1 distills (1.5B-14B) and Qwen3, we verify separability by testing that suppressing narration does not degrade a latent-answer probe while suppressing computation does, and that the effect holds on spontaneous chains of thought and production-style prompts, not only contrastively elicited ones. We show narration activation stays high during overthinking after residual work reaches zero, and intervene both mid-reasoning and at generation time. We report deployment value (tokens, wall-clock, cost) at equal accuracy against verbosity steering, TTS-style pruning, and reactive early-exit, with ablations isolating each construction step. The work reframes overthinking as an over-narration mode and offers a precise, interpretable efficiency mechanism.
Experiments:
Compute fits an academic node (<= 8xA100-80GB). Primary model: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, frozen; only linear probes are trainable, interventions are activation projections. Scale sweep: R1-Qwen distills 1.5B/7B/14B and Qwen3-8B. Decoding: temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, max 16k thinking tokens, seeds 0/1/2 on every reported number. CoT segmented into steps; analysis restricted to extractable-answer items (math / multiple-choice). Datasets, used as released: GSM8K test (1319), MATH500 (500), AIME 2024+2025 (60), GPQA-Diamond (198); a held-out 300-problem set (disjoint from evaluation) is used to build the subspaces. A subset of everyday/production-style prompts is included to test that effects are not artifacts of curated reasoning sets.

Experiment 1 (H1 - Constructing the narration subspace, with ablated construction): Collect contrastive activation pairs by prompting the model to render the SAME worked computation tersely vs verbosely on the held-out set; compute per-layer difference-of-means and assemble a low-rank narration subspace by SVD; orthogonalize against the answer-probe directions. Build an alternative narration signal from easy-vs-hard problems. Construction ablations: (a) terse-vs-verbose contrast only, (b) orthogonalization only, (c) random subspace of the same rank, (d) reproduced single verbosity direction. Decisive metric: variance explained and rank of the narration subspace, and principal-angle alignment between the terse/verbose subspace and the easy/hard subspace, plus alignment to the single verbosity direction (for the collapse criterion). Convincing: a low-rank (<= 10-dim) subspace captures the contrast and aligns with the easy/hard signal (principal angles < 45 degrees), while retaining >= 3 dimensions not aligned with the single verbosity direction. Indecision: alignment in [45, 60] degrees. Negative (no low-rank structure or > 60 degree misalignment): a stable narration subspace cannot be constructed.

Experiment 2 (H1 - Separability from computation): Train a linear latent-answer probe on 40% of held-out problems; evaluate on 60%. Compare probe accuracy under (a) projecting out the narration subspace, (b) a matched-rank random subspace, (c) the computation subspace (answer-probe weights). Report principal angles between narration and computation. Decisive metric: latent-answer probe accuracy drop under narration removal vs. computation removal. Convincing: narration removal drops probe accuracy < 3 points (comparable to random) while computation removal drops > 20 points, with narration/computation principal angles > 60 degrees. Indecision: narration-removal drop in [3, 8] points or angles in [45, 60] degrees. Negative (narration removal drops probe > 8 points or not near-orthogonal): the subspaces are not separable, refuting H1.

Experiment 3 (H2 - Narration stays high after computation completes, on spontaneous CoT): Read narration-subspace activation magnitude at each step of SPONTANEOUS (not contrastively elicited) chains of thought; measure residual work via truncate-and-resume. Decisive metric: out-of-sample 5-fold R^2 of the post-completion narration-activation integral predicting wasted tokens, minus best competitor among trace length, single verbosity-direction projection, and a confidence probe. Convincing: narration stays significantly elevated after residual work hits zero and its post-completion integral beats the best competitor by >= 0.10 R^2 on at least three datasets. Indecision: advantage in [0.02, 0.10]. Negative (<= 0.02 or no sustained activation): overthinking is not specifically sustained narration.

Experiment 4 (H3 - Mid-reasoning and generation-time projection: is narration truly post-hoc?): Subtract the projection onto the narration subspace at selected layers, applied (i) only at generation-time end-phase and (ii) DURING intermediate reasoning; if narration is post-hoc presentation, mid-reasoning suppression should cut tokens without harming the latent answer, whereas suppressing computation mid-reasoning should. Coefficient and layers selected on the held-out construction problems; full accuracy-vs-token Pareto reported. Systems compared on all four datasets: narration-subspace projection vs. (a) no intervention, (b) single verbosity/length steering (ASC/Manifold-style), (c) TTS-style post-hoc pruning, (d) Reasoning-Theater-style probe early-exit, (e) fixed truncation matched to mean budget. Decisive metric: token reduction at equal accuracy, with the key comparison whether narration projection Pareto-dominates the single verbosity direction (>= 5% more reduction at matched accuracy) - and the pre-registered COLLAPSE test (extra dimensions add < 5% over the single direction => idea reduces to length steering). Secondary: mean tokens, accuracy, wall-clock latency, per-query cost. Convincing: >= 25% token reduction within 1 point on GSM8K and MATH500, strictly above the single-direction frontier. Indecision: reduction in [10%, 25%] or within 5% of the single direction (collapse regime) - the separability analysis (Experiments 1-2) is then the standalone contribution. Negative (< 10% or worse than single direction): the subspace method adds nothing.

Experiment 5 (H3 - Qualitative: shorthand, not damage): Under narration suppression, an LLM-judge plus human spot-check (200 traces, two annotators) rate whether derivation steps are preserved while decorative narration/verification asides are dropped. Decisive metric: fraction of suppressed traces preserving all load-bearing derivation steps. Convincing: >= 85% preserve load-bearing steps while dropping narration, kappa > 0.6. Indecision: [70%, 85%]. Negative (< 70%): suppression damages computation.

Experiment 6 (H3 - Controls and underthinking): Control for prompt style, answer difficulty, and token budget; on the hardest quartile where narration may overlap genuine verification, measure accuracy drop vs. suppression strength. Decisive metric: hard-item accuracy drop at the deployed coefficient, and stability of savings across prompt styles/difficulty. Convincing: hard-item accuracy drops < 1 point at the coefficient delivering Experiment-4 savings, savings stable across prompt styles. Indecision: 1-3 point drop. Negative (> 3 point drop): narration suppression harms genuine verification, bounding H3.

Experiment 7 (H1/H3 - Generality across data, scale, and family): Transfer the narration subspace across datasets and the 1.5B/7B/14B/Qwen3-8B models (>= 2 families) without recomputation. Decisive metric: separability asymmetry (Experiment-2 probe-drop) and token savings under a transferred subspace, relative to in-domain. Convincing: transferred subspace retains the separability asymmetry and >= 80% of in-domain savings on at least three scales. Indecision: 60-80% retention. Negative (< 60%): the narration subspace is idiosyncratic across models.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The clean separation of narration and computation may not hold - verification/narration can carry genuine computation, so suppression might harm hard problems; this trade-off is measured directly and a near-null separability result is itself informative. Contrastive terse/verbose prompting may not match spontaneous overthinking; we mitigate with an easy-vs-hard alternative signal and explicitly test on spontaneous CoT and production-style prompts. Latent-answer probes are reliable mainly for extractable answers, so we restrict to math/multiple-choice. The narration subspace may collapse into the single verbosity direction, in which case the pre-registered collapse criterion fires and the dimensional framing yields little gain over prior steering (the separability analysis remains a contribution). Projection at generation time can push activations off-distribution; coefficient sweeps and validity checks address this. Deployment adopters are reasoning-model servers and agent frameworks that pay per token; the mechanism must beat simpler early-exit/length steering to be adopted, which Experiment 4 tests head-on. Results may be model-family and scale specific.
